sentences.text: Namaskar.
Sutra 10 makes it very clear that the mystical experience is not cut off from sense experience.
On the contrary, all the senses are transfigured and transmuted into the supreme consciousness,
which is compared to the sun and its rays, which are nothing but divine energies.
Ananda Shaktipada introduces the Sutra in the following way, quote.
Having revealed the system of the oral teaching concerning the four deities in the previous Sutra,
now he will explain the secret of the psyche of the twelve currents.
Vada Shabha Chakra Rahasya.
Sutra 10
Vada Shabha Udayena Maha Marici Vikasara.
By the rise of the twelve currents, there occurs expansion of the great rays of consciousness.
Commentary.
The five cognitive senses, beginning with hearing, along with the mind,
and the five senses of action, beginning with speech, along with the intellect,
are the twelve currents as they arise collectively.
Their radiant manifestation, ul-lasa, constitutes the current of the all-absorbing consciousness spontaneously,
without any cause, by their mode of action of supreme freedom, without any constraint,
in the absolute stillness of the luminous abode.
By that flow, there happens an expansion of the great rays of consciousness, unobstructed,
within the flow of each of the senses,
takes the form of upsurge, manifestation, regime, consumption, and repose.
These are the five phases of Khamma, which we have encountered before,
Utyuga, Avabhasa, Charvana, Anangrasa, and Vishwanti.
This is the great awakening, Mahaprabhata,
by the dissolution of the perception of all distinctions,
such as what is restricted and unrestricted, conscious and inert, being of ever-absorbing nature.
Being ever indestructible, it is established everywhere and at all times.
This is the meaning of the great saying, end of the quote.
The sutra is here called Mahavakya, like the fundamental sentences of the Upanishads.
Calling this a great awakening shows that the process is only complete
when there is not only introversion, but also expansion into the cosmic consciousness,
which is indestructible.
Swami Lakshman too has accepted a different reading of the sutra,
Vadasya Vaha Ulla Sena instead of Udayena, in the Kashmir edition.
But the meaning does not differ much.
His translation reads, quote,
By giving rise to twelvefold flow of energies,
the expansion of supreme energy,
the preeminent Svatanthya Shakti prevails.
And his commentary throws much light on the applicability of this sutra.
Quote,
Though these twelvefold flows are verily twelvefold experiences
from five senses of action, five senses of cognition, mind and intellect,
yet we have to make it possible in such a way
that these very experiences are transformed in Ullasa,
the upward flow of Shakti.
Only in that case, Maha Mariji Vikasar,
expansion of the supreme energy will surely take place.
The entire range of these flows of energy
is virtually the expansion of one Shakti
defined as Maha Mariji or Svatanthya Shakti in scriptures,
who is the all-inclusive one infinite Shakti of the supreme being.
When all the senses are transformed in the formation of energy
in the super-god consciousness state,
whatever we see with these gross eyes,
we see the supreme being shining before us.
In the same way,
other senses too get transformed
from the state of senses to the energies
and the expansion of Svatanthya pervades all around.
End of the quote.
That the senses are called flows or currents
is already true in the natural condition,
where they are flowing out
towards their respective objects of perception.
At the next higher stage,
the yogi internalizes this externalizing tendency
and he makes them merge in the heart center.
This is what happens in the Kattlobanishad,
the famous mantra,
Paranchi Karni da Trima Tsvayambhu,
that the creator has made these openings
towards the outer external.
But some sage has come
and he turned it with him,
Avrita Chakshu,
he turned the eyes with him
and attained the Atman directly.
This is the stage of internalizing.
Without a complete and stable internalization,
no progress can be made.
It is the third and highest stage
which has been expressed in the brevity of this sutra.
Here, the yogi makes this flow rise,
hence Udaya or Ulasa,
as the reading may be.
And instead of being held in internal absorption,
the senses become transformed
into divine energies.
And thus, it is not only the yogi
or mystic who attains perfection,
but his divinized senses
attain the state of pure consciousness
which radiates throughout the universe.
